chapter: World's Greatest Jazz Band and Denver
title: Brazil and the bossa nova
summary: He toured Brazil with Ella and the WGJB, learned the bossa nova beat, and discusses Charlie Byrd and Stan Getz.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Well, listen, then you were just mentioning that tour of Brazil. That was with Ella, huh?
Well, I made it with Ella first, and then later with the World's Greatest Jazz Band.
Did the World's Greatest Jazz Band go down to Brazil?
Oh, yes.
They did?
We went to Rio and Sao Paulo.
Yeah, because they don't hear that much jazz, but they're very enthusiastic.
Oh, they love it. They loved it.
I don't guess that many records are available to them.
Over there?
Yeah.
You know, they have records that we don't have.
Oh, do they?
Records -- you'd be surprised.
Is that right? Is that right?
From the States.
Fancy that.
Like, with Ella, I went to a party and this guy -- I forget his name, but he had us over to his house.
Yeah.
And he had records from this wall to that side.
Is that --
All the way, nothing but jazz records.
Fancy that.
And I'm telling you, you go to mostly any of them's home they got nothing but records.
Gus, did you -- did those rhythms strike you?
Oh, yes, before the bossa nova came
over, well, I learned it over there.
Oh, you did?
The bossa nova beat, sure, I did. I went there with Ella.
Oh.
After we got back then the bossa nova came over.
Became big.
That's right.
But you brought it back, in a sense.
Well, somebody else brought it back, but it became a big hit then, right after we got back.
Was it Herbie Mann that --
No, no.
Oh, it was prior to that, wasn't it?
No, a guitar player from Washington.
Not -- oh, not Charlie --
Charlie Byrd.
Charlie Byrd.
Charlie Byrd.
Oh, he brought it back then, huh?
His drummer was playing the bossa nova beat.
Is that right?
And also, Stan Getz, they made a big
hit with it.
That's right, they did.
But that was Charlie Byrd's date.
No kidding.
And Stan Getz got his name on that.
Wow.
Sure.
How did that happen?
They used him because -- I don't know why but that's the way it happened.
There must have been a lot of dollars involved there.
Well, something happened, there almost was a lawsuit against [them.]
Oh, was there?
Yeah.
How about that?
Yeah. But he was a good --
